findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no rollback path
findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_referral_code;
findings.why_it_matters: The column and its data are gone permanently, and a deploy rollback cannot restore them. Any still-running old application instance that selects that column will also start erroring mid-deploy.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two releases: stop reading the column, ship, then drop it in a later migration.

findings.title: Archive-then-delete is not atomic and not idempotent
findings.evidence: DELETE FROM accounts WHERE last_seen_at < now() - INTERVAL '2 years';
findings.why_it_matters: The INSERT and DELETE are separate statements with no transaction, so a failure between them deletes accounts that were never archived. now() also moves between runs, so a re-run acts on a different row set — unlike the CREATE statements above, which are correctly guarded.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap both statements in a transaction and pin the cutoff to a fixed timestamp.
